1.5 Recommended reading routes
For the signal processing route, read integer addresses, the Hilbert bridge, FIR transfer, faithful filter
banks, and Haar packets. For the adaptive route, read known edges, mask perturbations, complete
prunings, the dynamic program, and its stability envelope. For the algebraic route, read formal cyclic
products, homogeneous Smith actions, and CRT masks.
Every displayed code excerpt is copied from an immutable source declaration. The raw excerpt, its
source line range, and its SHA256 hash accompany the PDF. Excerpts rely on the imports, namespaces,
variables, and definitions in their source files. They are not advertised as independently compilable
snippets. The complete project remains the authoritative executable object.
2 Partitions, signed addresses, and the Hilbert bridge
2.1 A packet first means a coordinate mask
Take an index set 𝐼, a label set 𝑅, and a phase map 𝜙∶𝐼→𝑅. The packet with label 𝑟keeps coordinate
𝑖exactly when 𝜙(𝑖) = 𝑟:
(𝑃𝑟𝑥)(𝑖) = {𝑥(𝑖),
𝜙(𝑖) = 𝑟,
0,
𝜙(𝑖) ≠𝑟.
The definition requires a zero in the value type and a decidable label equality. It does not require a
Fourier transform, a measure, or an inner product.
Source: KomorebiPaperV/Packets.lean.
def packet (phase : I →R) (r : R) (x : I →V) : I →V :=
fun i => if phase i = r then x i else 0
Applying the same mask twice changes nothing. Distinct labels cannot both be retained at the same
coordinate. If the label type is finite and values can be added commutatively, the finite sum of packets
returns the original value. At any one coordinate exactly one summand survives.
Source: KomorebiPaperV/Packets.lean.
theorem packet_complete (phase : I →R) (x : I →V) (i : I) :
(∑r : R, packet phase r x i) = x i := by
classical
calc
(∑r : R, packet phase r x i) = packet phase (phase i) x i := by
apply Finset.sum_eq_single (phase i)
· intro b _ hb
simp [packet, Ne.symm hb]
· simp
_ = x i := by simp [packet]
The proof uses Finset.sum_eq_single to isolate the surviving label. This simple mechanism is reused
after stronger ambient structures are introduced.

7.8 Dyadic and odd masks factor by CRT
If 𝑁= 2𝑎𝑀with 𝑀odd, the two factors are coprime. An integer satisfies a residue condition modulo
their product precisely when it satisfies both factor conditions. The source proves the corresponding
equality of integer-residue masks.
Source: KomorebiPaperV/CRT.lean.
theorem dyadic_odd_packet_factorization (a d : ℕ) (hd : Odd d)
(r : ZMod (2 ^ a * d)) (x : ℤ→V) :
KomorebiPaperV.packet (fun i : ℤ=> (i : ZMod (2 ^ a * d))) r x =
KomorebiPaperV.packet (fun i : ℤ=> (i : ZMod (2 ^ a)))
(ZMod.chineseRemainder (dyadic_odd_coprime a d hd) r).1
(KomorebiPaperV.packet (fun i : ℤ=> (i : ZMod d))
(ZMod.chineseRemainder (dyadic_odd_coprime a d hd) r).2 x) :=
residue_mask_factorization _ _ (dyadic_odd_coprime a d hd) r x
This is an exact mask factorization. It does not prove that a particular nonuniform sample allocation
is optimal, nor does it provide a minimax sampling theorem. It supplies the arithmetic structure on
which more specialized sampling constructions can be built.
8 Trust boundaries and reproduction
8.1 What the inherited audit actually checks
The preserved compiler log records 225 explicit theorem targets and 827 namespace declarations. The
audit driver first requires each target to be present as a theorem. It then traverses the KomorebiPape
rV namespace, rejects unsafe declarations, rejects local axiom and opaque declarations, and collects
transitive axiom dependencies.
Only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound are permitted. The audit checks the dependencies
of the compiled declarations. It does not prove that English prose is a correct paraphrase of those dec-
larations, that a Python implementation matches a Lean definition, or that an application has supplied
a theorem’s hypotheses.
The current guide build reconciles each target name with its immutable source location and in-
herited axiom-output record. It verifies pinned source hashes and performs a lexical scan for proof
placeholders and prohibited source constructs. These checks protect provenance and locate obvious
source-policy violations. They do not replace elaboration, type checking, or a new kernel traversal.
8.2 The two dates of evidence
The release’s raw kernel verification timestamp is 6 September 2026 at approximately 03:18 UTC. This
monograph companion is dated 9 October 2026. The compiler transcript describes the preserved v1.1.0
sources and their pinned dependencies. Its date remains visible beside the current checks.
The recorded computational review ran the twenty exact model tests, comprising 305,933 counted
assertions, and all sixteen verifier control methods. It ran the 33 current companion pytest tests and
the 27 overlapping historical tests with no skips. These are finite tests of implementations and models,
with separate contracts for their tested scope.

This copies the complete authored guide tree to an isolated directory and compiles the supplied TeX
and generated catalog files in four passes. It executes no Lean code and does not regenerate mathemat-
ics. The separate build_guide_data.py script can regenerate the catalogs when supplied the immutable
release root and the traditional edition’s final crosswalk. It verifies hashes and rejects mismatched con-
tracts before writing the guide’s data products.
The raw excerpt files preserve source text. Their rendering files escape TeX-special characters and
route rare mathematical glyphs to a suitable font. The PDF is a reading surface. The full source files
retain the actual namespace and typeclass context needed for Lean compilation.
8.7 A checklist for using the theorems
Before using a result, identify its ambient type and explicit hypotheses, locate the exact declaration, and
check how the application supplies each hypothesis. For an FIR bank, confirm finite Laurent support
and delay units. For a transform equality, supply weighted summability. For pruning synthesis, supply
conservation. For selector stability, establish the strict gap and joint local-error bound. For a Smith chart,
check denominator nonvanishing or use the projective action.
This is the recurring pattern of the formal development: construct the object in the correct space,
prove the bridge to the intended model, then use the identity whose hypotheses have actually been
supplied.

11.5 Building this reading guide
From the directory for the editable Lean guide, run python3 build.py. It compiles the supplied TeX
and excerpt files with XeLaTeX and does not invoke Lean or regenerate mathematical evidence. The
build uses installed URW P052 and Nimbus Sans, Latin Modern mono and math, and DejaVu Sans
Mono fonts. Font files are resolved locally with kpsewhich and standard system locations, then copied
only into the private build stage. No font binaries are bundled or downloaded. The monograph style is
supplied beside the TeX source. The script copies the full authored guide tree to a temporary directory
and compiles it in four passes. No installation is performed. verify_pdf.py performs the documented
PDF checks and renders all pages into contact sheets.
assemble.py is a separate step for generating documentation. It reads the preserved source snap-
shot, exact source contract, selected excerpt list, and a current verification report. Its default inputs
are relative to the supplied package. It also accepts --source and --verification paths when those
inputs are stored elsewhere. Its generated tables are already supplied for ordinary PDF reproduction.
Run python3 reconcile_sources.py to check those tables and excerpts against the preserved sources
without changing their mathematical content.
11.6 When a reuse needs a new proof
Before adapting an endpoint, check the scalar field, finite versus bounded setting, positivity notion,
time domain, evidence condition, and domain/codomain of every operator. Changing a hypothesis
is not a formatting edit. A new theorem about unbounded generators, general statistical sufficiency,
infinite hidden-state elimination, or unrestricted Banach holomorphic calculus requires its own proof
and correspondence review. The preserved project supplies a precise starting point for that work.

1.4 How to read a proof script
The scripts repeatedly use a small set of proof moves. rw replaces an expression using a stated equality.
simp only performs a controlled reduction with an explicit list of lemmas. The broader simp tactic
also uses the available simplification database. ext i j reduces a matrix equality to equality of each
entry. funext proves equality of functions by comparing values. constructor starts the two obligations
of a conjunction or equivalence. rintro decomposes quantified and existential data. obtain names an
existential witness already proved to exist. refine fixes the overall shape of a term and leaves specified
holes to prove.
The tactic noncomm_ring normalizes ring expressions without commuting factors. It is appropriate
for identities involving 𝑃𝑏𝑈𝑃𝑎. Ordinary ring is used for scalar arithmetic or commutative coefficient
expressions. A normalization step must therefore be read in the ring where it is used. It does not permit
arbitrary matrix factors to be reordered.
A line beginning have proves or names a local intermediate assertion. The goal remains the same
until that assertion is used. A calc block presents a chain of equalities or inequalities. Each link is a
separate obligation. Induction on a list proves all finite circuit depths, including the empty list. A finite
example verified by norm_num or fin_cases proves that concrete example, not a theorem in arbitrary
dimension.
For a derivative identity, HasDerivAt.unique often supplies the final step: two proven derivatives
of the same function at a point must coincide. The script first differentiates a product, then rewrites
the product as a constant or as a known function, then invokes uniqueness. Thus the differentiated
projector and unitary identities are derived from actual functions and their derivatives, rather than
postulated as unrelated data of first order.
1.5 Scope is a part of the theorem
The finite results have broad mathematical scope, but their hypotheses also place clear limits on their
use. A statement about the span of an algebra orbit permits every matrix in that algebra. Reachability
under a physically specified set of unitary gates requires a separate argument. A theorem establish-
ing complete positivity for finite channels quantifies over every finite reference index. Arbitrary infi-
nite reference Hilbert spaces lie outside those declarations. A derivative computation under supplied
smoothness does not prove the existence of a Schrödinger solution for every initial condition.
The modules for the projected connection do use arbitrary smooth real parameter manifolds and
complete normed model spaces, which is broader than a single finite-dimensional chart. This gener-
ality of the mathematical parameter space is distinct from the paper’s unproved continuum physics
conjectures. Neither the word “manifold” nor an estimate in an abstract C-star algebra supplies a con-
tinuum tower, a physical constraint algebra, a renormalized limit or a Lorentzian emergence theorem.
Read each conclusion under its actual hypotheses and use its source locator to recover the surround-
ing assumptions. Source identity and excerpt fidelity are current documentation checks. Saved com-
piler and axiom transcripts are inherited proof evidence. This distinction continues through the replay
chapter and full result map.

The complete theorem catalog includes seven declarations from the constraint audit, four Schur–

11.5 Historical counts, failures, and numerical mirrors
The historical verification appendix records six successive proof blocks. Its earlier coverage and
remaining-work lists describe those stages. The sixth ledger supplies the cumulative finite correspon-
dence. These records preserve what each stage established. The active source is the 392-declaration
sixth-block branch. The earlier 298-declaration branch was not merged into it.
The sixth development record retains 31 captured checks, 21 of which failed before correction. Those
diagnostics and source snapshots are separate from the accepted cumulative build. The invalid equality
and admitted-proof controls were rejected in that accepted run. A failed development attempt is not a
theorem. A corrected theorem is assessed through its active source and accepted evidence.
The inherited sixth numerical mirror records 182 factor pairs, 638 truncation cases, 3,190 arbitrary
rank-bounded competitors, nine invalid-input controls, and two assumption-removal controls. It uses
NumPy complex128 and numerical rank thresholds. It is neither extracted nor compiled Lean and
does not prove universal matrix optimality. Any present numerical rerun is reported separately in the
edition’s verification records. The historical CPU/GPU benchmarks were not rerun here, and their
recorded comparison fields do not automatically instantiate the complete formal fair-match signature.
11.6 Reproducible limits
The three companions share the original result keys and preserve the complete raw mathematical and
formal sources. The paper-to-Lean map explains recorded hypotheses and scope. It is not an automat-
ically checked semantic-equivalence theorem between prose, Lean, and prototype Python. No fresh
CUDA correctness, device stability, timing advantage, full imported-library rebuild, or claims beyond
the stated finite mathematics follow from the documentation checks.

The triangular inverse identities hold over arbitrary commutative rings, so they apply in particular
over the p-adic integers.
Example 10.20 (First-order sign and error precision). For p = 2, s = 0, M = 2, F(Y, T) = Y + T, H = 1,
a = 0, and v = 1, the prescribed parameter is τ = 4 and the solved root is y = −8. Here J = K = 1,
and the forcing term is H(a) + Kv = 2. Omitting the parameter term would predict −4, and reversing
its sign would predict 0. The corresponding errors −4 and −8 are both outside 22MZ2 = 16Z2. Thus
either change would violate the stated error bound.
The error exponent cannot uniformly be increased. For F(Y, T) = Y + Y2 + T, H = 0, a = 0, p = 2,
s = 0, M = 1, and v = 1, there is an even root y of y + y2 + 2 = 0. Its equation forces y ≡2 (mod 4)
and y + 2 = −y2, so
4 | y + 2,

Thus the error depth 2M −3s = 2 is attained even for parameter-only motion. The same quadratic
with a constant coefficient perturbation gives the coefficient-only boundary. These examples refute a
uniform extra error digit. They do not assert optimality for every individual choice of p, s, M.
The combined results establish finite singular obstructions, smooth compatible towers, full con-
tinuous root charts after a suitable coordinate choice, and quantitative deformation for a rationally
invertible solved Jacobian. Rationally rank-deficient persistence remains a separate problem. The
analytic solution-map theorem in the next section supplies the regularity conclusion for these same
derivative blocks.

12 Open questions and further directions
The arithmetic results above resolve Nishibuchi’s conjecture throughout its stated parameter range. The
local analyticity and differentiability theorem is also complete under its stated invertibility hypothesis.
What remains is a set of extensions and sharper classifications, together with the broader questions
raised by the original native seed-calculus program.
12.1 Singular persistence beyond an invertible solved block
The weighted lifting theorem allows the solved Jacobian to be noninvertible modulo p provided that
it is invertible over Qp with a controlled inverse. This includes a substantial class of lifts often called
singular modulo p. The next problem is to understand Jacobians that remain rank-deficient over Qp,
where the inverse construction is no longer available.

The finite obstruction theorem decides whether this set is empty from the residual digit and reduced

The conclusion concerns one level: vanishing of the obstruction permits the next step, but does not

We seek structural hypotheses and higher obstruction data that control an entire singular branch,
including its behavior under coefficient and parameter deformation. One route is to propagate suitable
conditions from level to level. Another is to prove existence at all levels in a form that yields compatible
branches. The finite obstruction calculus supplies the tests for individual levels, but a persistence
theorem needs a further argument linking them. Any general formulation must allow multiple branches,
later obstructions, and changes in the rank of the Jacobian.

A reader contract for this edition
Chapter XI develops packet decomposition, finite representation comparisons, actual arithmetic/type adapters,
and a conditional comparison interface. This guide makes the logical boundaries visible in the source language.
The mathematical text gives the exposition. The visual guide illustrates the constructions. The retained Lean
sources provide the formal statements and proofs at their printed hypotheses.
The general arithmetic realization endpoint is presented as Conjecture 66. Conjecture 66 isolates the missing
realization claim from historical Claim 16.2, indexed as original obligation 66. This separation preserves the
proved finite comparison and the proved conditional implication. It records that finite assembly and coherent
transport have not yet supplied an actual supercuspidal realization in the original generality.
The accompanying release includes Markdown (.md) files containing detailed proofs, construction notes,
proof audits, and research records. These documents distinguish established results, conditional results, and
the remaining obligations associated with Conjecture 66.
1.1 What Lean certifies
Acceptance by Lean checks that the declared conclusion follows from its binders, imported declarations, and
foundational axioms. It does not silently instantiate a local field, an arithmetic type, a reference correspondence,
or a normalized local-factor convention. Those objects must appear in the source or in a separate mathematical
attachment.
A structure may contain an existence field. A theorem that consumes that structure proves an implication using
the field. It is still a substantive theorem when the comparison map, descent or uniqueness is constructed. It is
not a proof of the structure’s arithmetic existence. In particular, Realization.exists_atom is an existence input
in the formal comparison interface.

Given that same π and realization witness, the conditional comparison proposition assumes original H5 for
